<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">1-bit AI Infra: Part 1.1, Fast and <span id="id1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#D9D9D9;">Lossless</span> 
<br class="ltx_break">BitNet b1.58 Inference on CPUs </h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent advances in 1-bit Large Language Models (LLMs), such as BitNet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite> and BitNet b1.58 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>, present a promising approach to enhancing the efficiency of LLMs in terms of speed and energy consumption. These developments also enable <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">local LLM</span> deployment across a broad range of devices. In this work, we introduce <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#D9D9D9;">bitnet.cpp</span>, a tailored software stack designed to unlock the full potential of 1-bit LLMs. Specifically, we develop a set of kernels to support <span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">fast</span> and <span id="abstract1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">lossless</span> inference of ternary BitNet b1.58 LLMs on CPUs. Extensive experiments demonstrate that bitnet.cpp achieves significant speedups, ranging from 2.37x to 6.17x on x86 CPUs and from 1.37x to 5.07x on ARM CPUs, across various model sizes. The code is available at <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/BitNet" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">aka.ms/bitnet</a>.</p>
  
</div>
<figure id="S0.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2410.16144v2/m2_performance.png" id="S0.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/327;" width="476" height="327" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>Comparison of <span id="S0.F1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">inference speed</span> and <span id="S0.F1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">energy consumption</span> for various <span id="S0.F1.7" class="ltx_text">BitNet b1.58</span> model sizes on an Apple M2 Ultra (ARM CPU) using llama.cpp(fp16) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite> versus bitnet.cpp (ternary kernels). The results demonstrate that bitnet.cpp can achieve human reading speed, even for a 100B model on a single CPU. Notably, bitnet.cpp significantly reduces energy consumption across different model sizes.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>bitnet.cpp</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">bitnet.cpp is an inference framework for 1-bit LLMs (e.g., <span id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">BitNet b1.58</span> models). It provides <span id="S1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">lossless inference</span> while optimizing both <span id="S1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">speed and energy consumption</span>. The initial release of bitnet.cpp supports inference on CPUs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As illustrated in Figure <a href="#S0.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1-bit AI Infra: Part 1.1, Fast and Lossless BitNet b1.58 Inference on CPUs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, bitnet.cpp achieves speedups ranging from 1.37x to 5.07x on ARM CPUs, with larger models experiencing greater performance
gains. Additionally, it reduces energy consumption by 55.4% to 70.0%, further boosting overall efficiency. On x86 CPUs, speedups range from 2.37x to 6.17x with energy reductions between 71.9% and 82.2%. Furthermore, bitnet.cpp can run a 100B <span id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">BitNet b1.58</span> model on a single CPU, achieving speeds comparable to human reading (5-7 tokens per second)<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>, thus significantly enhancing the potential for running LLMs on local devices.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To start using bitnet.cpp for inference, follow these steps:</p>
</div>

<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Optimized Kernels for 1.58-bit Models</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">bitnet.cpp offers a suite of optimized kernels, including I2_S, TL1 and TL2. The kernels are designed for fast and lossless inference of 1.58-bit models on both x86 and ARM architectures.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.T1" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S2.T1.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S2.T1.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S2.T1.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_l ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S2.T1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Unpack</span></td>
<td id="S2.T1.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S2.T1.2.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pack</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S2.T1.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S2.T1.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_l ltx_border_r ltx_border_t">-1</td>
<td id="S2.T1.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_t">00</td></tr>
<tr id="S2.T1.2.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S2.T1.2.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_l ltx_border_r ltx_border_t">0</td>
<td id="S2.T1.2.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_t">01</td></tr>
<tr id="S2.T1.2.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S2.T1.2.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_b ltx_border_l ltx_border_r ltx_border_t">1</td>
<td id="S2.T1.2.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_b ltx_border_r ltx_border_t">10</td></tr>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>I2_S Kernel transforms each full-precision weight into a 2-bit value to save memory and bandwidth. When performing computation, the 2-bit weights are unpacked to the original values.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">I2_S Kernel</span> adopts the vanilla multiply-then-addition manner to perform the matrix multiplication. As shown in Table <a href="#S2.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 2 Optimized Kernels for 1.58-bit Models ‣ 1-bit AI Infra: Part 1.1, Fast and Lossless BitNet b1.58 Inference on CPUs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, it transforms each full-precision weight into a 2-bit representation offline. During computation, it transforms the weights back to their original values and performs the vanilla GEMV operations.
We recommend using it with sufficient threads, since it allows the compiler to generate efficient pipelined instruction sequences.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.T2" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S2.T2.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S2.T2.2.1" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S2.T2.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_r ltx_border_t">
<span id="S2.T2.2.1.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:42.7pt;">
<span id="S2.T2.2.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="S2.T2.2.1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pack</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S2.T2.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S2.T2.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_l ltx_border_r ltx_border_t">

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span>TL1 Kernel transforms every two full-precision weights into 4-bit index and performs LUT computation.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TL1 Kernel</span> preprocesses every two full-precision weights by packing them into 4-bit index (see Table <a href="#S2.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 2 Optimized Kernels for 1.58-bit Models ‣ 1-bit AI Infra: Part 1.1, Fast and Lossless BitNet b1.58 Inference on CPUs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), and pre-computes their corresponding activations into <math id="S2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3^{2}=9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^{2}=9</annotation></semantics></math> values. The index-value pairs are stored in a lookup table to perform LUT computation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>. GEMV processing is performed using an int16 LUT and accumulation through addition. We recommend using it with a limited number of threads when serving large models.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.T3" class="ltx_table">

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>TL2 Kernel compresses every three full-precision weights into a 1-bit sign (<span id="S2.T3.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF0000;">0</span> or <span id="S2.T3.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF0000;">1</span>) and a 4-bit index. </figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TL2 Kernel</span> is similar to TL1. The major difference is that it compresses every three weights into a 5-bit index, while TL1 compresses every two weights into a 4-bit index. Therefore, TL2 achieves a higher compression ratio than TL1. We recommend using it in environments with limited memory or bandwidth, since it employs LUT and reduces model size by 1/6 compared to TL1 Kernel, thereby lowering bandwidth requirements.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Evaluation</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Inference Performance</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluated bitnet.cpp in terms of both <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">inference speed</span> and <span id="S3.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">energy cost</span>. Comprehensive tests were conducted on models with various parameter sizes, ranging from 125M to 100B. specific configurations for each model are detailed in the Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Model Config ‣ 1-bit AI Infra: Part 1.1, Fast and Lossless BitNet b1.58 Inference on CPUs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>. These sizes represent popular LLM configurations. Additionally, systematic tests were performed on both ARM and x86 architectures. For ARM, we used a Mac Studio with an Apple M2 Ultra processor and 64GB of memory for end-to-end tests. For x86, a Surface Laptop Studio 2 with an Intel Core i7-13700H processor (14 cores, 20 threads) and 64GB of memory was used.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We tested two scenarios for each device: one with inference limited to two threads, and the other without thread restrictions, reporting the optimal inference speed. It was to consider the limited thread availability on local devices, providing a more accurate performance assessment of <span id="S3.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">BitNet b1.58</span> in local environments.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Inference Speed:</span> Table <a href="#S3.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 3.1 Inference Performance ‣ 3 Evaluation ‣ 1-bit AI Infra: Part 1.1, Fast and Lossless BitNet b1.58 Inference on CPUs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and Table <a href="#S3.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 3.1 Inference Performance ‣ 3 Evaluation ‣ 1-bit AI Infra: Part 1.1, Fast and Lossless BitNet b1.58 Inference on CPUs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> demonstrate significant performance advantages of bitnet.cpp over llama.cpp on both ARM (Apple M2) and x86 (Intel i7-13700H) architectures, especially as model sizes increase. bitnet.cpp consistently outpaces llama.cpp, with speedups ranging from 1.37x to 6.46x, depending on the model and architecture. On the Apple M2, speedups peak at 5.07x in the unlimited thread scenario, while on the Intel i7-13700H, bitnet.cpp achieves up to 6.46x in thread-limited scenarios, making it particularly effective for local inference on resource-constrained systems.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The performance gap widens as models scale up, with larger models (13B and above) benefiting the most from bitnet.cpp’s optimizations. On the Intel i7-13700H, bitnet.cpp provides substantial speed improvements, making it well-suited for x86 architecture, even with limited threads. While smaller models (125M to 1B) also see meaningful gains, the advantages of bitnet.cpp become especially critical for larger, more complex models, underscoring its efficiency in handling demanding workloads. Adding to the observed performance differences, bandwidth limitations play a significant role in the varying efficacy of bitnet.cpp across different architectures, particularly when comparing the Apple M2 and Intel i7-13700H. Due to the larger bandwidth of the Apple M2, it achieves significantly faster speed improvements with bitnet.cpp compared to the Intel i7-13700H, especially when running larger models.</p>
</div>

<td id="S3.T4.2.1.6.12" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;"><span id="S3.T4.2.1.6.12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">2.44</span></td>
<td id="S3.T4.2.1.6.13" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;"><span id="S3.T4.2.1.6.13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1.70</span></td></tr>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 5: </span>Comparison of inference speed across different CPUs (Unit: Tokens/Second) in a thread-limited setting, where the number of available inference threads is set to 2. "N/A" indicates that the tested CPU cannot host the specified model size with the given kernel.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Energy Cost:</span> We ran 700M, 7B and 70B models and reported the energy cost (J/token) with the best inference speed in the unlimited thread setting. Table <a href="#S3.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 3.1 Inference Performance ‣ 3 Evaluation ‣ 1-bit AI Infra: Part 1.1, Fast and Lossless BitNet b1.58 Inference on CPUs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> demonstrates a clear advantage of bitnet.cpp in reducing energy consumption. For the Apple M2, bitnet.cpp reduces energy usage by 55.4% to 70.0% depending on the model size. As model size increases, bitnet.cpp’s energy efficiency becomes more pronounced, with the largest model (70B) showing a 70.0% reduction in energy consumption compared to llama.cpp. This highlights bitnet.cpp’s ability to deploy large-scale inference more efficiently, both in terms of speed and energy usage, which is crucial for energy-constrained environments such as mobile devices or edge computing.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">On the Intel i7-13700H, energy savings with bitnet.cpp are even more dramatic, ranging from 71.9% to 82.2% for models up to 7B. Although energy consumption data for the 70B model on the Intel CPU is unavailable, the results for smaller models clearly show that bitnet.cpp can significantly lower the energy demands of large language model inference on high-performance, multi-core processors.</p>
</div>

<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Inference Accuracy</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The bitnet.cpp framework enables lossless inference for ternary <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">BitNet b1.58</span> LLMs. To evaluate <span id="S3.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">inference accuracy</span>, we randomly selected 1,000 prompts from WildChat <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite> and compared the outputs generated by bitnet.cpp and llama.cpp to those produced by an FP32 kernel. The evaluation was conducted on a token-by-token basis, with a maximum of 100 tokens per model output, considering an inference sample lossless only if it exactly matched the full-precision output.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This evaluation used a 700M <span id="S3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">BitNet b1.58</span> model<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            We used <a href="https://huggingface.co/1bitLLM/bitnet_b1_58-large" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">bitnet_b1_58-large</a> available on HuggingFace to demonstrate the inference capabilities of bitnet.cpp. This model and the 8B <span id="footnote1.2" class="ltx_text">BitNet b1.58</span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite> in the quick start were <span id="footnote1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF0000;">neither trained nor released by Microsoft</span>.</span></span></span>. The results confirm that bitnet.cpp achieves accurate, lossless inference for 1-bit LLMs.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T7" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S3.T7.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S3.T7.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S3.T7.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;" rowspan="2"><span id="S3.T7.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Kernel</span></td>
<td id="S3.T7.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;" colspan="2">llama.cpp</td>
<td id="S3.T7.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;" colspan="3">bitnet.cpp</td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T7.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S3.T7.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;">TQ1_0</td>
<td id="S3.T7.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;">TQ2_0</td>

<td id="S3.T7.2.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;">TL1</td>
<td id="S3.T7.2.2.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;">TL2</td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T7.2.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S3.T7.2.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;">Accuracy</td>
<td id="S3.T7.2.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;">1.4%</td>
<td id="S3.T7.2.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding-top:1pt;padding-bottom:1pt;">1.4%</td>

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7: </span>Comparison of inference accuracy between llama.cpp and bitnet.cpp. TQ1_0 and TQ2_0 are kernels in llama.cpp, while l2_S, TL1, and TL2 are kernels in bitnet.cpp. Accuracy indicates the proportion of lossless inference samples, where outputs matched exactly with the full-precision baseline.</figcaption>

</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Future Work</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We are expanding bitnet.cpp to support a broader range of platforms and devices, including mobile devices (e.g., iPhone and Android), NPUs, and GPUs. We will also work on 1-bit LLM training optimization in the future. Furthermore, we are interested in the co-design of customized hardware and software stacks for 1-bit LLMs.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Acknowledgement</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">

Additionally, we extend our thanks to our colleagues and fellow interns at Microsoft Research Asia for their invaluable discussions and feedback. In particular, we acknowledge Jiangyu Wei, Shijie Cao, and Ting Cao for introducing the LUT method for low-bit LLM inference on CPUs in their T-MAC work. Xiaoyan Hu provided extensive system and device support, as well as insightful discussions on operating system integration.</p>

<p id="A1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">We hope the release of bitnet.cpp will inspire the development of 1-bit LLMs in large-scale settings in terms of model size and training tokens.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Statement of Contribution</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All co-authors contributed to discussions, provided input on various aspects of the project, and assisted with experimental design, paper writing, and resource coordination. In addition to these contributions, J. Wang and T. Song crafted multiple kernels and laid out the overarching architecture for the BitNet inference framework. J. Wang took on the full task of kernel implementation. H. Zhou invested considerable time running experiments focused on inference speed, accuracy, and energy consumption.</p>
</div>
</section>
</article>

      support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
      methods listed below:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"
            height="1em" viewBox="0 0 640 640">
            <path
              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
